newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan to tender for 66,000T of U.S. wheat-traders.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to tender for 66,000T of U.S. wheat-traders.

text.p: Taiwan is expected to tender for up to 66,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat next week, while corn and soybean buyers are sidelined as demand slows down going into the summer season, traders said on Friday.
The Taiwan Flour Mills Association is expected to place a tender late next week for two 33,000-tonne U.S. wheat shipments, the traders said.
"The association is still working on its final details, but it should place the tender late next week," a Taipei grain trader told Reuters by telephone.
Taiwan corn and soybean buyers would take a wait-and-see attitute and remain sidelined next week due to a general slowdown in the market, traders said.
"Demand is weak, so buyers are all waiting for either a sharp futures price fall or improved domestic demand," a buyer at Taiwan's Hui Shung Group said.
The Hui Shung Group had passed on a tender about two weeks ago for 8,000 tonnes of corn and 46,000 tonnes of soybeans.
The buyer for group said the shipment would not be retendered until July.
The Hui Shung buyer said their decision was based mainly on expectations of lower Chicago futures prices and the slower pace of demand in the summer.
"The slow summer is ahead of us and July soybean contracts still may test 800 U.S. cents (a bushel) support," he said.
Corn buyers will probably also remain quite in the coming week as most of the buying groups have covered their needs until September, traders said.
